title: 1987 AHSME Problem 2
statement: As shown in the figure, a triangular corner with side lengths \(DB=EB=1\) is cut from equilateral triangle \(ABC\) of side length \(3.\) The perimeter of the remaining quadrilateral \(ADEC\) is

solutions.text:
Since \(\angle DBE=60^\circ\) and \(DB=EB=1,\) triangle \(DBE\) is equilateral, so \(DE=1.\) The original perimeter is \(9.\) Cutting off the corner removes two unit segments and adds one: \[ 9-1-1+1=8. \]

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Start from the original perimeter, remove \(BD\) and \(BE,\) and add \(DE\)
